retired: Retired on 2026-11-20 by ADR 0006 (docs/adr/0006-internet-access-through-a-named-tunnel.md), decision D19 of the remote-access spec. The checks dns-public, tls, redirect, sse, nginx-test and cert-issuer fail by design once the console name moves to a Cloudflare tunnel. This file is kept as a record and is no longer a goal manifest of any epic. Its results stay in docs/plans/2026-11-19-local-name-evidence.md.

goals.outcome: A device that asks Cloudflare DNS gets the PC address for the console name, and the PC asks no DNS server that deletes the answer.
https://<name> opens the console with a certificate that every device trusts, and http://<name> goes to the HTTPS address.
Live updates work through nginx: the events stream delivers its first lines, and a started loop shows Running in 2 seconds.
Port 7070 is closed to the network, and the console still works on the PC.
Behind a reverse proxy the sign-in works over HTTPS with a Secure cookie, live updates arrive, and each device has its own count of failed sign-ins.
Startup shows the address to open.

checks.run: npx vitest run --project api tests/api/sign-in-startup.test.ts tests/api/cli.test.ts -t "public-url"

goals.outcome: The nginx configuration in the repository holds every proxy rule and the file names that win-acme writes, and nginx accepts it.
No own issuer is trusted on the PC, and none of its files is on the PC.
The certificate comes from Let's Encrypt and is renewed without a person (parts b and c need an administrator and are recorded in the N3 evidence).
